tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
tools.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only Routines that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1+131	valid Fortress program, an expression's runtime type is always a subtype of
2+131	its static type.
3+131	We say that a value is \emph{an instance of} its runtime
4+131	type and of every supertype of its runtime type; immediate subtypes of
5+131	\TYP{Any} comprises of tuple types, arrow types, \TYP{()}, and \TYP{Object}.
6+131	
7+131	The exclusion relation is a symmetric relation between two types
8+131	whose intersection is \TYP{BottomType}.
9+131	Because \TYP{BottomType} is uninhabited
10+131	(i.e., no value has type \TYP{BottomType}),
11+131	types that exclude each other are disjoint:
12+131	no value can have a type that is a subtype of two types that exclude each other.
13+131	\note{
14+131	The converse is technically not true: we can define two traits with
15+131	 method declarations
16+131	 such that no trait or object can extend them both, so no value can have a
17+131	 type that is
18+131	 a subtype of both trait types, but the trait types do not exclude each
19+131	 other.  For example:
20+131	 trait A f(self, y: Object) = 1; end
21+131	 trait B f(x: Object, self) = 2; end
22+131	 trait C f() = 3; end
23+131	
24+131	No pair of the three trait types defined above can be extended
25+131	but none of them exclude any of the others.
26+131	}
27+131	Note that \TYP{BottomType} excludes every type including itself
28+131	(because the intersection of \TYP{BottomType} and any type is \TYP{BottomType}),
29+131	and also that no type other than \TYP{BottomType} excludes \TYP{Any}
30+131	(because the intersection of any type $T$ and \TYP{Any} is $T$).
31+131	\TYP{BottomType} is the only type that excludes itself.
32+131	Also note that if two types exclude each other
33+131	then any subtypes of these types also exclude each other.
34+131	
35+131	
36+131	Fortress also allows \emph{coercion} between types
37+131	(see \chapref{conversions-coercions}).  A coercion from $T$ to $U$
38+131	is defined in the declaration of $U$.  We write $T \coercedefto U$ if
39+131	$U$ defines a coercion from $T$.  We say that $T$ \emph{can be coerced
40+131	to} $U$, and write $T \coercesto U$, if $U$ defines a coercion from
41+131	$T$ or any supertype of $T$: $T \coercesto U \iff \exists T':

== libbuild.sh
#!/bin/bash
# usage: libbuild.sh ; honours FORTRESS_CACHES and FORTRESS_ANALYZER_CLAUSES_CACHE from the environment
cd /home/user/fortress-memo/ProjectFortress
for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
  s=$(date +%s.%N)
  ../bin/fortress compile $f ; rc=$?
  e=$(date +%s.%N)
  printf '@@TIME %s rc=%s %.1f s\n' "$f" "$rc" "$(echo "$e - $s" | bc)"
done
== ctdiff.sh
#!/bin/bash
# usage: ctdiff.sh <outdir> <names-file> ; compiles each named compiler_tests unit (names from ct-names.py), one capture per unit
out=$1; names=$2; mkdir -p $out
cd /home/user/fortress-memo/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests
for t in $(cat $names); do
  o=$out/$(echo $t | tr / _).txt
  if [ -f $t.fss ] ; then src=$t.fss ; elif [ -f $t ] ; then src=$t ; else echo "NOFILE $t" > $o ; continue ; fi
  timeout 300 ../../bin/fortress compile $src > $o 2>&1
  echo "rc=$?" >> $o
done
